title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: KENDRA'S WHISTLE
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Kendra Mills, a hospital billing clerk from Columbia, South Carolina.
Kendra hates arguments. She says sorry to furniture.
So of course, she ended up with the loudest job in town.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE DOOR
segments.quote: Courage is fear holding on a minute longer.
segments.author: George S. Patton
lines: Her brother Marcus runs a Tuesday night basketball league for men over forty. Bad knees, big opinions.
When their referee moved away, Marcus begged her to step in.
The first night, Kendra stood at the gym door, ready to run home.
Then she remembered General George Patton, on her dad's old coffee mug:
Courage is fear holding on a minute longer.
So she held on one more minute. Then she walked in.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE CROWD
segments.quote: Don't let the noise of others' opinions drown out your own inner voice.
segments.author: Steve Jobs
lines: Ten minutes in, everybody was yelling. Players, wives, one man's mother with a cowbell.
Kendra made calls just to stop the yelling. It got worse.
At halftime, a friend texted her a line from Steve Jobs:
Don't let the noise of others' opinions drown out your own inner voice.
In the second half, she called only what she saw.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE RULEBOOK
segments.quote: There's a lot of blood, sweat and guts between dreams and success.
segments.author: Bear Bryant
lines: She grew up with four brothers, so she thought she knew basketball. She did not know the rules.
Marcus gave her the rulebook, with a note from the coach Bear Bryant taped inside:
There's a lot of blood, sweat and guts between dreams and success.
So she read it every lunch break, and watched old games at night.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE BAD CALL
segments.quote: Mistakes are always forgivable, if one has the courage to admit them.
segments.author: Bruce Lee
lines: In week six, she called a foul on Big Lou, a retired mail carrier. Lou never touched the guy.
Lou yelled for a full minute. Kendra wanted to hide under the bleachers.
Then she thought of Bruce Lee, the martial arts legend:
Mistakes are always forgivable, if one has the courage to admit them.
So she said it out loud. I got that one wrong, Lou. The gym went quiet. Then Lou laughed.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: HER BROTHER
segments.author: Benjamin Disraeli
lines: The championship came down to one last shot, taken by her own brother.
Marcus pushed a guy. Everyone saw it. Everyone looked at Kendra.
She remembered Benjamin Disraeli, the old British prime minister:
Justice is truth in action.
She blew the whistle. Foul on Marcus. His team lost. He skipped the gravy at Sunday dinner, just to make a point.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE JACKET
segments.quote: Friendships born on the field of athletic strife are the real gold of competition. Awards become corroded, friends gather no dust.
segments.author: Jesse Owens
lines: Next Tuesday, Big Lou handed her a black jacket. It said Ref Kendra on the back.
The whole league chipped in. Especially Marcus.
Lou said Jesse Owens put it best:
Friendships born on the field of athletic strife are the real gold of competition. Awards become corroded, friends gather no dust.
Now Kendra trains new referees. Lou brings the snacks.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Hold on. Hear yourself. Do the work. Own it. Be fair. Make friends.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Hold on one more minute. Hear your own voice. Do the work. Own your mistakes. Be fair. Make friends.
I tried to referee my family's Thanksgiving once. I'm still in the penalty box.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
